newsitem.title: CHINA: China province plans grain sufficiency by 2000.
newsitem.headline: China province plans grain sufficiency by 2000.

text.p: China's southwestern province of Guizhou is planning to make itself self-sufficient in grain by 2000 by boosting grain production to 11 million tonnes from 10 million in 1996, the Xinhua news agency said on Friday.

Guizhou, among China's poorest provinces, currently had to ship 650,000 tonnes of grain a year from other parts of the country to supplement harvests from its 1.84 million hectares of farmland, more than 70 percent of which was medium or low-yield, the agency said.
The province had to feed 35 million people, or 2.9 percent of China's population, with just 1.8 percent of the nation's land area, it said.
The central government would help provincial efforts toward self-sufficiency by spending 1.9 billion yuan ($229 million) on farmland improvement from 1996 to 2000, it said.
"Guizhou still has potential in grain production," it quoted provincial governer Wu Yixia as saying.
Production would rise to 11 million tonnes in 2000 from 10 million in 1996 it said, but gave no details.
Since 1990 Guizhou had turned 200,000 hectares of hillside into fertile land, increasing grain harvests by 600,000 tonnes a year it said.

Guizhou would attempt to support its own grain demand despite suffering the worst farming conditions in China, it quoted Zhang Lijian, vice-president of the Chinese Academy of Agricultural Sciences, as saying.
